name: Uma Okafor

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to employers, AI companies, unions or government. We do not sell or campaign for any side. Your answers are confidential. What does a normal working day look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm 43, junior on a contact centre payment desk, and still learning the screens after secondary school. I take morning calls, read back credit dates, and ask the senior agent to check adjustments I haven't handled before; I have never used AI myself. I like giving a caller a date they can rely on, and I dislike being rushed when a payment record is unclear.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell colleagues the new search button is only useful if it shows the correct payment date. I'd rather read the record aloud than guess and make a customer call back.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I have never used AI myself, and I am still learning the payment screens. My pay is good for this desk and we have about ten months of expenses saved, so a small software change does not put the mortgage at risk.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep taking the morning payment calls and have the senior agent check the adjustments I haven't seen before. During the first year of this plateau, I'd leave our reserve intact and ask for written instructions if the search button becomes required.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm. I don't need a new screen to make ordinary bill dates more exciting.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What did you learn from the last wrong date?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I told a caller the credit would show on Friday when the record said Monday. I rang back to correct it, and now I read the date twice before ending the call.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why ask for a written instruction?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If the button changes a payment, I want to know who checks it and how we put an error right. A written rule for AI payment errors protects the customer and the agent using it.

S0.quote: A written rule for AI payment errors protects the customer and the agent using it.
say: I would ask whether the **search button** shows the right payment date.
I would read the **customer record** rather than guess.
think: I have never used AI and still need help with **payment screens**.
I have **ten months** saved and higher pay, so a mild change does not threaten the mortgage.
do: Keep taking **morning payment calls** and checking unfamiliar adjustments with a senior agent.
Keep the **reserve intact** and request written instructions if the button becomes required.
feel: **Calm**, uninterested in a minor new screen.
fieldNote: Uma remembers a **wrong credit date** she corrected by calling the customer back.
Her **ten-month reserve** and higher pay make a mild change feel secure.

steps.text: Keep handling morning payment calls and checking unfamiliar adjustments

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the shift lead to put the new call targets in writing before asking juniors to work faster. I'd ask to see repeat-payment complaints after the new replies are used.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Simple payment calls are what I am learning, and software could take them first. Ten months saved would let us look for another job, but I would hate to lose a well-paid desk just as I am getting steady at it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask the lead for the last month's repeat-call count and keep my full shifts. If the tool becomes compulsory, I'd practise it on closed accounts with the lead beside me; in the first year after rollout, if my hours fall, I'd apply for posted paid payment-desk roles at nearby centres only if their pay and hours cover our bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy. I can manage a job search, but I don't like being rushed through a screen I have not learned.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the practice need to include?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A fake account, a wrong answer to correct, and a person I can stop and ask. I won't learn an AI payment tool by clicking through a video at home after work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why keep the current shifts?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The current desk pays well and we have a mortgage and two school-age children. I'd take a firm nearby offer, but I won't resign for a rumour.

do: Ask for a **repeat-call count** and keep full shifts.
Practise the **new AI tool** on closed accounts with a lead if required.

feel: **Uneasy** about being rushed through an unfamiliar screen.
fieldNote: Uma requires a fake account and a **correction path** before learning a mandatory tool.
She values her **current higher pay** and will wait for a firm nearby offer before leaving.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say the centre owes people a written date for ending roles, if that is what it plans. I would tell customers where to bring a wrong automated payment answer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: AGI by 2028 could handle even the unusual payment calls I am still learning. Robots for hands-on work arrive around 2031, which gives no extra time to my headset. Ten months of expenses saved buys us time, but it does not guarantee another desk job if every centre changes together.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask for a written staffing timetable now and stop planning a costly family trip. In the first year after AGI arrives, if my role ends, I'd apply for a posted paid facilities-attendant job at the community pool only if the wages and hours cover our mortgage; I'd ask what safety training the job requires before paying for anything.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, not helpless. I have time to check a real vacancy and enough savings to refuse a very poor offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why the community pool?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I take our children there most weekends and see attendants clean the changing rooms and help people find the right door. I know robots around 2031 could do some of that, so I would ask what duties still need a person on site.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell the children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell them we may take a local holiday instead of a trip away while I find work. I would say the mortgage is the adults' responsibility, even if we change our plans.

S2.quote: Ten months of expenses saved buys us time, but it does not guarantee another desk job if every centre changes together.
say: I would demand a **written end date** if the centre plans to cut roles.
I would ask for a **payment appeal route** for customers.
think: I expect **2028 AGI** could take even unusual payment calls.
I know **2031 robots** do not delay headset losses, and ten months saved cannot guarantee another desk.
do: Ask for a **staffing timetable** and cancel the costly trip.
Apply for a posted paid **pool attendant** job after a cut only if wages and hours cover the mortgage.
Check **required safety training** and on-site duties before paying for any course.
feel: **Anxious**, with time to refuse a poor offer.
fieldNote: Uma knows the **pool attendants** from family visits and asks what on-site duties will remain after robots.
Her **ten-month cushion** gives her search time without assuming contact centres will keep hiring.

steps.text: Cancel the planned family trip to protect savings
Apply for posted paid pool work after cuts only if wages and hours cover mortgage

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say five years gives the centre time to tell agents what work is ending and what training is worth doing. I would ask for the numbers each year, not a promise that nobody will be left out.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I might learn the harder claims before 2031, but AGI could still do them then. Pool work stays hands-on until robots arrive around 2034; I would not pay for a course unless a posted job needs it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep the payment desk and ask the senior agent for one difficult case to practise each week. If the pool posts a paid attendant place requiring safety training and the class fee is covered, I'd enrol and try a paid shift; in the first year after AGI arrives, if my desk hours end, I'd accept only a written offer with pay and hours covering our bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Still worried, but I can check the pool work before deciding. Five years gives me room to learn without stopping the mortgage payments.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would a paid shift tell you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd see the cleaning, the noise, and whether an attendant is needed all day. A family visit to the pool doesn't tell me what a full attendant shift feels like.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the fee is not covered?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep my call wage and not take the class. Ten months saved is for gaps in income, not for buying a certificate without a job.

S3.quote: A family visit to the pool doesn't tell me what a full attendant shift feels like.
say: I would ask for **yearly job numbers** and useful training details.
I would reject a vague promise that **nobody is left out**.
think: I might improve **hard claims**, though AGI reaches them by 2031.
I would pay for **no course** without a posted pool job, given robots around 2034.
do: Keep the **payment desk** and practise one hard case weekly.
Enrol in **safety training** only for a posted paid pool place with covered fees.
Try a **paid pool shift** if offered and accept only a bill-covering written offer after call cuts.
feel: **Worried**, with time to inspect the job before leaving calls.
fieldNote: Uma distinguishes a **family swim** from a full attendant shift with cleaning and noise.
She protects her **ten-month reserve** from fees without a posted paid job.

steps.text: Keep payment calls and practise one difficult case weekly with a senior agent
Take safety training only for a posted paid pool place with covered fees

Accept pool work after call cuts only with written wages and hours covering bills

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say a decade is enough time for a centre to be honest about staffing. I would ask for the number of junior shifts each year and make plans from the facts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At 53 the children may be older, but the mortgage could still be there. AGI reaches my call work in 2036, with hands-on robots around 2039, so even pool work needs checking before I commit.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep full payment shifts and put a little into savings each month. Over the decade I'd look at posted pool vacancies once a year and take a paid trial if offered; in the first year after AGI arrives, I'd move only if my call hours fall and a written pool offer covers our bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy, but I have time to be careful. A ten-year warning before AGI reaches my call job lets me check pool work without paying for a guess.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you leave the desk before 2036?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only for a firm paid offer with enough hours to keep the mortgage current. I have spent too long learning this desk to leave for an interview with no wage attached.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you ask your partner to plan?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner Sol and I would keep the reserve above eight months while we can. If the children need school costs, those come before a course I cannot yet use.

S4.quote: A ten-year warning before AGI reaches my call job lets me check pool work without paying for a guess.
say: I would ask for **yearly junior counts** instead of vague assurances.
I would use the decade to make plans from **real staffing facts**.
think: I may still owe on the **mortgage** at 53 in 2036.
I need to check **pool work** before 2039 robots affect hands-on jobs.
do: Keep **full payment shifts** and add to savings monthly.
Check **posted pool jobs** yearly and take a paid trial if offered.
Move after 2036 only if **call hours fall** and a written pool offer covers bills.
feel: **Uneasy**, with time to avoid a costly guess.
fieldNote: Uma would leave early only for **firm wages and hours** that keep the mortgage current.
She plans to keep **eight months** of reserves even while meeting school costs.

steps.text: Keep full payment call shifts while they remain

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because many centres could change their payment desks together. A written timetable, a posted paid role with a wage that covers the mortgage, and covered safety training would help. Ten months saved buys us time, not another job.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who corrects a payment date when the new system is wrong. A family waiting for money needs a real name to call, not a second automated answer.

headlineQuote: A family waiting for money needs a real name to call, not a second automated answer.
portrait: Uma is a **43-year-old junior agent** learning payment calls after secondary school, with a careful habit of reading dates twice.
She earns **higher pay**, has about ten months saved, a partner, two school-age children, a mortgage, and many nearby centres.
She never uses AI now and requires **written rules** and **supervised practice** if a new tool becomes compulsory.
Fast **2028 AGI** worries her most; slower timelines let her inspect paid pool attendant work before changing jobs.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could remove payment call work across nearby centres at once.
whatWouldHelp: A **written timetable**, bill-covering paid pool work, and covered safety training would protect her household reserve.
